summary: This paper compares two Ti3C2Tx MXene electrodes/films: Al−Ti3C2 prepared from an excess-Al Ti3AlC2 precursor and conventional Ti3C2 prepared from a conventional precursor. Both materials were etched with an HF/HCl mixture and delaminated using LiCl; the Al−Ti3C2 material was the headline, best-performing sample. No electrochemical capacitance, electrolyte, current-density, scan-rate, or mass-loading data were reported because the study evaluates conductivity and environmental/thermal oxidation stability rather than energy-storage performance. Al−Ti3C2 freestanding films reached electronic conductivities exceeding 20 000 S/cm, while fresh Al−Ti3C2 flakes had reported average lateral sizes of 1.3 to 1.6 μm.
